nameStory: This moss earned the name 'thyme-moss' because its tiny, oval leaves arranged in neat patterns reminded early botanists of the herb thyme's foliage. The 'woodsy' part refers to its preference for growing in forested areas rather than open spaces. Some folks also call it 'baby-tooth' moss because the leaf edges have tiny teeth-like serrations that are just visible with a magnifying glass.
description: Woodsy Thyme-moss is a small but noticeable moss that forms bright green patches in shady forest spots. It grows in low, spreading mats that hug the ground, rarely getting taller than your thumb. The individual plants have distinctly oval leaves arranged in neat rows, giving the moss a somewhat organized, almost quilted appearance that stands out from the more chaotic growth of many other mosses.

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Oval-shaped leaves with tiny teeth along the edges (visible with a hand lens) arranged in neat, overlapping rows like shingles on a roof

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Forms low, spreading mats that feel slightly springy underfoot and have an organized, quilted appearance rather than a tangled mess

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Bright emerald green when moist, becoming duller olive-green when dry, with a subtle glossy sheen in good light

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Feels soft and slightly cushiony to the touch, not crispy or brittle like some mosses, and springs back when gently pressed

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Almost always found at the base of trees, on rotting logs, or around rocks in rich, moist forest soil rather than in open sunny areas

habitat: Look for Woodsy Thyme-moss in rich, moist forests where it carpets the ground around tree bases, stumps, and moss-covered rocks. It particularly loves areas with good soil nutrients, like wet meadows that border forests, rich hardwood groves with maples and oaks, and the edges of forested wetlands. You'll find it from sea level up into the mountains, but it's most common in sheltered valleys and north-facing slopes.

seasonality.spring: The moss becomes vibrant emerald green as spring moisture returns, making it easiest to spot. New growth appears fresh and glossy.
seasonality.summer: Remains green and identifiable but may look duller during dry spells. The organized leaf pattern is most obvious now when growth is mature.
seasonality.fall: Often produces spore capsules on thin stalks rising above the moss mat. Color stays green but may become more muted.
seasonality.winter: Stays green under snow and is often more visible when deciduous leaves have fallen, revealing moss patches on tree bases.

funFact: This humble moss is actually nature's tiny pharmacy - scientists are studying its natural antimicrobial and antifungal compounds for potential medical uses, the same properties that make it perfect nesting material for songbirds and salamanders who want to keep their homes germ-free!
confusionNotes: Other thyme-mosses in the same genus can look very similar, but Woodsy Thyme-moss has the most organized, shingle-like leaf arrangement. Remember: 'Woodsy stays tidy' - its leaves are more neatly arranged than its messier cousins like Wavy-leaf Moss, which has more irregular, wavy-edged leaves.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called 'thyme-moss,' this plant isn't related to the cooking herb thyme at all - it's purely a visual comparison. The scientific name 'cuspidatum' means 'pointed,' referring to the leaf tips, while 'Plagiomnium' roughly translates to 'slanted moss' for the way the leaves are arranged.
compareHints: Among its thyme-moss relatives, Woodsy Thyme-moss has the most orderly, shingle-like leaf arrangement compared to Wavy-leaf Moss's more irregular, wavy-edged leaves. Alpine Thyme-moss is typically found at higher elevations, while Marsh Thyme-moss prefers wetter, more open wetland areas rather than forest floors. The neat, organized appearance of Woodsy Thyme-moss makes it the 'tidiest' member of the family.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Wavy-leaf Moss stands out from its thyme-moss relatives primarily by those distinctive wavy, toothed leaf margins - Woodsy Thyme-moss has smoother leaf edges, while Marsh Thyme-moss prefers wetter areas and has more pointed leaves.
Unlike its relatives Woodsy Thyme-moss (found in forests) and Marsh Thyme-moss (found in wetlands), Alpine thyme-moss is strictly a high-elevation specialist.
Compared to its relatives, Marsh Thyme-moss has the broadest, most elliptical leaves - Woodsy Thyme-moss has more pointed leaves, while Wavy-leaf Moss has distinctly wavy leaf edges.
